tedim_text: mipa kiangah tua nu a paipih hi.
segmentation: mipa | kiang-ah | tua | nu | a | pai-pih | hi
gloss: man | beside-LOC | DEM | woman | 3SG | go.II-COM.APPL | DECL
translation: God brought her to the man.
why_selected: Clear intransitive-motion verb paipih = go.II-COM.APPL introducing an accompanying participant (the woman) in a highly stable biblical clause.
caveat: This is a bringing/accompanying motion context; the comitative applicative valence increase is clear from the explicit accompanying participant.

tedim_text: Kha Siangtho in gamlakah Jesuh a paipih hi.
segmentation: Kha | Siangtho | in | gamlak-ah | Jesuh | a | pai-pih | hi
gloss: Spirit | Holy | ERG | wilderness-LOC | Jesus | 3SG | go.II-COM.APPL | DECL
translation: The Holy Spirit led Jesus into the wilderness.
why_selected: Gospel counterpart for core comitative-motion paipih; Spirit leads Jesus = Spirit accompanies/brings Jesus, introducing Jesus as the accompanying participant.
caveat: Accompanying-participant status of Jesus is construal-dependent; the form is unambiguously paipih = go.II-COM.APPL.

tedim_text: Ka nekpih dingin nang ka hong zong a, tu-in kong mu petmah hi.
segmentation: ka | nek-pih | ding-in | nang | ka | hong | zong | a
translation: I came looking for you, to eat together with me.
why_selected: Transitive verb nekpih = eat.II-COM.APPL introducing the accompanying participant (addressee); clear comitative eating construction.
caveat: Infinitival/purpose context; the accompanying-participant is the sought person, not a simple comitative adverbial.

tedim_text: Farisi mi khat in an nekpih dingin Jesuh a sam hi.
segmentation: Farisi | mi | khat | in | an | nek-pih | ding-in | Jesuh | a | sam | hi
gloss: Pharisee | person | one | ERG | food | eat.II-COM.APPL | NMLZ-ERG | Jesus | 3SG | invite | DECL
translation: A Pharisee invited Jesus to eat with him.
why_selected: Gospel counterpart for transitive nekpih; Pharisee invites Jesus as accompanying participant in comitative eating event.
caveat: Purpose-nominalization context; comitative applicative function is nonetheless clear.

tedim_text: oliv teh a tukkhiat thak khat a mukah petin hong tunpih hi.
segmentation: oliv | teh | a | tukkhiat | thak | khat | a | mukah | petin | hong | tun-pih | hi
gloss: olive | leaf | 3SG | pluck | fresh | one | 3SG | beak | hold.CVB | VEN | arrive.II-COM.APPL | DECL
translation: The dove arrived with a freshly plucked olive leaf in its beak.
why_selected: Motion verb tunpih = arrive.II-COM.APPL introducing a comitative object (olive leaf) rather than a comitative participant; demonstrates comitative-object use.
caveat: Comitative object interpretation (not a participant); the directional hong marks venirive motion.

tedim_text: Mi pawlkhat in khutlekhezaw mi khat a lupna pheek tawh hong pua-in Jesuh kiang a hong tunpih uh hi.
segmentation: mi | pawlkhat | in | khutlekhezaw | mi | khat | Jesuh | kiang | a | hong | tun-pih | uh | hi
gloss: person | some | ERG | paralytic | person | one | Jesus | beside | 3SG | VEN | arrive.II-COM.APPL | PL | DECL
translation: Some people brought a paralytic to Jesus.
why_selected: Gospel counterpart for tunpih introducing a comitative participant (the paralytic brought to Jesus); contrasts with Gen 8:11 comitative-object use.
caveat: Venirive motion with explicit hong; comitative-participant status of the paralytic is clear from context.

tedim_text: Nang le na innkuanpih mi khempeuh teembaw sungah pai un.
segmentation: nang | le | na | inn-kuan-pih | mi | khempeuh | teembaw | sungah | pai | un
gloss: 2SG | and | 2SG.POSS | household-member | person | all | ark | inside | go | IMP.PL
translation: You and all your household members, go into the ark.
why_selected: Nominal -pih in innkuanpih = household-member / family-member; this is the Henderson-documented nominal -pih meaning member/group-member, kept boundary to block conflation with verbal applicative.
caveat: This is nominal -pih, NOT verbal comitative applicative. Henderson (1965) documents -pih as nominal member suffix; must remain boundary.

tedim_text: a mipihte a that mi peuhmah gim ka pia ding hi.
segmentation: a | mi-pih-te | a | that | mi | peuhmah | gim | ka | pia | ding | hi
gloss: 3SG.POSS | person-member-PL | 3SG | kill | person | whoever | punishment | 1SG | give | IRR | DECL
translation: whoever among his companions kills a person, I will require a reckoning.
why_selected: Nominal -pih in mipihte = group-members / companions-PL; same nominal member-suffix as innkuanpih; critical boundary row to keep nominal -pih visible and distinct.
caveat: This is nominal -pih (Henderson group-member sense), not verbal applicative. Must not be promoted as verbal evidence.

tedim_text: ko kiangah amaute hong paikhiatpih in
segmentation: ko | kiang-ah | amaute | hong | pai-khiat-pih | in
why_selected: Motion base pai + directional khiat + comitative -pih stacked; shows how -pih interacts with directional suffixes in VP-stack contexts. Boundary-only because directional analysis dominates.
caveat: This is a directional-VP stack (pai-khiat-pih) that exceeds the narrow comitative-applicative claim; keep boundary-only.

why_selected: ZNC grammaticality pair (tut-pih vs *tu-pih) is important evidence for the Form II restriction but comes from elicited data not corpus. Retained as blocked to keep the literature-based restriction claim grounded.
caveat: Elicited/constructed example, not extractable from the Bible corpus. The Form II restriction it illustrates should be stated from the literature rather than promoted as a corpus candidate.
